## The week at a glance

| Day | Lesson | Superpower gained |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Import/Export + Tidy Data](day1-import-tidy.qmd) | any table in, tidy table out; pivots & joins in both dialects |
| 2 | [The Grammar of Wrangling](day2-verbs.qmd) | dplyr's 6 verbs ↔ the pandas method chain |
| 3 | [Visualization](day3-visualization.qmd) | the 5 charts that matter, grammar vs imperative |
| 4 | [Algorithm Gym #2](day4-gym2.qmd) | two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums |
| 5 | [Statistics + Project 2](day5-stats-project2.qmd) | the test battery + a reproducible statistical report |

## The rhythm of every day (~1–2 hrs)

1. **Cheat sheet** — 60–90 seconds of scanning, top of each lesson
2. **Lesson** — prose + live examples, both dialects
3. **Drills** — ~12 one-liners in a live pad; predict out loud, then run
4. **Exercises** — 5–6 graded, each with hint + solution (attempt first!)
5. **Common pitfalls** — real bugs, most caught in real analyses
6. **Self-quiz** — 5 predict-the-output questions; answers collapsed below

## Ground rules for the week

1. **Tidy first, analyze second.** 80% of "statistics problems" are data-shape problems
2. Every analysis step is a **verb** (R) or a **method chain** (Python) — no row loops
3. Plots get **titles and axis labels** before they're allowed in a report
4. Every random step gets a **seed** — the reproducibility thread starts today
5. End-of-week checkpoint: Project 2 — the same EDA + statistical report in both
   languages, with **identical numbers**

## The Week 1 → Week 2 bridge

Week 1 gave you data structures and functions. Week 2 is where those live on real
tables: the peptide assay you cleaned in Project 1 comes back on Day 5, and you'll
run the full statistical battery on it — distributions, t-tests, ANOVA, χ²,
regression — and ship it as a rendered Quarto report with `set.seed` and session
info, exactly the way a real analysis is handed off.

## Drill rule

Predict the output **out loud** before running any cell. Being wrong on
purpose is the fastest refresher there is.
